correctness.rationale: Odd G-Lehmer inputs are squarefree. For three primes, the local Gaussian-Euler factors give Phi(n) >= 64n/125, while n >= 105 gives F(n) <= n+1 < 2 Phi(n); divisibility therefore forces equality. Expansion with signed primes yields xy+xz+yz=x+y+z. The two uniform-sign cases are impossible; each mixed-sign case rearranges to one displayed quadratic factorization, and elementary size bounds force both factors positive. Reversing the algebra proves both converses. The packaged verifier independently agrees with the classification on every three-prime product through 5,000,000.

value.rationale: The theorem closes the natural three-prime layer immediately beyond the published semiprime classification, replaces a table of examples by an exact finite divisor parametrization, and proves that the source paper's odd proper-divisor problem cannot have a counterexample before four distinct prime factors. This is a structural restriction on the open problem, not merely a larger computation.
